title: High-Stakes Bouts and Performance Under Competitive Pressure in Mixed Martial Arts
abstract: Abstract: This study examines the impact of competitive pressure on performance in mixed martial arts using Ultimate Fighting Championship data from 2010 to 2021 (3,694 fights; 1,478 fighters). Fixed-effects logit models estimate how win probability changes after consecutive losses, controlling for ranking differences, physical characteristics (height, reach, age), and fighter fixed effects. The fighters were more likely to win after prior defeats. The odds of winning were 1.23 times higher after one loss ( p < .01) and 1.46 times higher after two consecutive losses ( p < .01), compared to fighters not on a losing streak. This pattern is consistent with adaptive adjustment under pressure. Gender differences emerged in the magnitude of these effects, although the small female subsample limits the generalizability of the gender-specific findings. The results suggest that performance under pressure reflects a combination of psychological, physical, and contextual factors. These findings may have implications for psychological preparation in high-stakes competition.

journal.name: Journal of Applied Sport and Exercise Psychology-Zeitschrift fur Sportpsychologie
